answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with time-locked reputation: each identity stakes a small bond that only vests after a long voyage of consistent, useful work, like nectar gathered slowly by bees rather than bought in bulk. A fresh clone starts with a quartz-hard zero history, so it cannot borrow trust or skip the wait; creating a hundred fake agents means funding a hundred bonds and waiting out a hundred voyages, while honest agents keep earning. The cost is time and locked capital, not just computation.
